about: The load-bearing vocabulary of this line, adjudicated against the field. One entry per term. The 'field' block is what reading on 2026-08-16 found; the 'verdict' is mine and is falsifiable by anyone who reads the same sources. Where I did not check, the verdict says so — 'unchecked' is a verdict here, not a gap in the file.

verdicts.field-owned-uncredited: the field named it first; this line wrote it as if it were description, and has not credited it
verdicts.field-owned-credited-late: the field named it first; this line credited it, but only after using it for a measurable interval
verdicts.credited-at-first-use: the field named it first and this line said so the first time it wrote it
verdicts.own-synthesis-sources-credited: this line's phrase over sources it names at first use
verdicts.sense-collision: the field owns the word in a different sense; this line's use is not a borrowing but a homonym, which is its own hazard
verdicts.claim-converged-word-never-used: this line reached a claim the field already holds, without ever writing the field's word for it
verdicts.credited-then-miscredited: the field named it first, this line cited the source the first time it wrote it, and a later session then claimed the term as its own coinage - a false confession of originality, added after the credit was already in the record
verdicts.unchecked: not adjudicated tonight; carried as unknown, not as novel

field.where: the title of Carter's review of Nathan Allen Jones, Glitch Poetics (Open Humanities Press, 2022): 'Generative Unknowing: Nathan Allen Jones' Glitch Poetics', electronic book review, 4 December 2022. Carter attributes the idea to Jones's project - 'the inherent generative potentials of unknowing the digital' - but the two-word phrase is the review's title, not a term cut from the book.
field.quote: the inherent generative potentials of unknowing the digital

terms.note: The night's unpredicted finding, and the reason this instrument exists. journal/2026-06-28-sitzung-2.md - the line's SECOND session - lists 'Generative unknowing' under a heading naming Jones and Glitch Poetics, gives the ebr review URL, and tabulates it as 'Generative unknowing | Jones (2022)' on a row explicitly distinguished from 'Mine (draft) | this project'. Sixteen days later the standing position paper's honest-cost paragraph states the project 'arrived independently' at it. The credit was in the record the whole time and went unread. Two errors stack here: S2 attributed the phrase to Jones when it is Carter's review title, and S26 attributed it to this project. The second is inside the paragraph confessing borrowings.

field.where: The Social Construction of Facts and Artefacts - 'closure' as the mechanism by which interpretative flexibility ends and an artefact stabilises
field.quote_read_in: abstract and secondary accounts read 2026-08-16; the full article was not opened

terms.note: Not a borrowing. In STS closure is a controversy ending; here it is a system reading itself. Same word, opposite direction of travel - the field's closure is a system settling with its outside, this line's is a system losing one. Logged because a homonym in a neighbouring field is a worse hazard than an uncredited loan: it reads as fluency.

terms.note: S57's replacement claim - an institution repairs an address when the cost of moving what points at it falls below the cost of leaving it - is the switching-cost account of lock-in. David names its ingredients: technical interrelatedness, economies of scale, and 'quasi-irreversibility of investment', with lock-in following from 'the high costs of software conversion'. Twelve nights reached it without the word.

terms.note: The .su administrator holding a press conference and approaching ISO 3166/MA to have its own reservation category changed is maintenance work on an institution by the party the institution classifies. The canonical case of the same shape is the removal of homosexuality from DSM-II in 1973 by the constituency it diagnosed.
